text:
maria: Heads up — onboarding sample app (quickstart-js) still uses the old `ApiKeyClient` constructor and encourages storing the token in plaintext README. That's a credential footgun.

maria: example from README:```js
const client = new ApiKeyClient('sk-...'); // <-- copied by users
```

maria: we had a support ticket where a customer pasted that into a public repo and later had to rotate keys.

li: ugh. I saw that too — our new SDK exposes `fromEnv()` helper and `rotateableCreds()` but the snippet wasn't updated.

derek: thanks for flagging. Is this just README, or also the sample app repo?

maria: both. quickstart-js repo still shows the same pattern in src/index.js and the README code block.

olivia: can we swap to `REDDIT_INFERENCE_API_KEY` style env var example and show `process.env` + `fromEnv()`? small PR should do it.

li: I'll open a tiny PR to update README and sample snippet. Will add a note about never committing keys and include `.env.example`.

maria: also add a short footnote recommending KMS/HSM for enterprise and link to the security page.

derek: assign to li and olivia for review. @li can you include a one-line migration note for older users who still call `new ApiKeyClient()`? Something like: "If you're using older samples, rotate keys and switch to the `fromEnv()` helper."

li: yep. PR in a minute. I'll also add a test that checks README codeblocks for `sk-` literals.

olivia: nice — that prevents regressions. Use a simple grep in CI.

ci-bot: build queued for branch update/readme-credential-footgun (job 4521)

li: CI passed, PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/quickstart-js/pull/201 — updates README, sample src, adds .env.example, and a short security blurb.

maria: thx! Can someone push a docs site patch as well? The SDK quickstart on docs.redwoodai.com still embeds the old snippet.

olivia: I'll take docs. Will update the static snippet generator and file a follow-up to sync all quickstarts.

docs-bot: docs site updated for /sdk/js/quickstart in next deploy.

derek: great. Follow-up items: (1) add lint/grep check to devex CI to catch literal keys, (2) audit other language quickstarts for similar footguns, (3) publish a short postmortem in #devex describing the fix.

maria: I'll draft the postmortem and ping support to notify affected customers to rotate keys.

li: closing the thread once docs patch is live. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
